subject.title: refactor(protocol): pre-publish cheat-window cleanup and vintage tracking

question: Should the gateway-protocol publication window permit these breaking export and schema removals, with the proposed `since` metadata becoming part of the generated public contract?
rationale: The patch is deliberately changing the pre-publication compatibility boundary; source review can confirm implementation consistency but cannot establish the intended package/API promise for beta and future npm consumers.

options.title: Approve the pre-publication break
options.body: Confirm the shipped-surface audit is sufficient and treat the reshaped schemas, removed exports, and generated vintage metadata as the new supported contract.

options.title: Preserve a migration surface
options.body: Retain the affected exports or provide a named compatibility/deprecation path for any beta or external consumers that must continue to build.

options.title: Split publication policy from cleanup
options.body: Land only the internal dead-code cleanup and defer externally visible protocol reshapes until package-versioning policy is documented.

recommendation.title: Approve the pre-publication break
recommendation.body: Confirm the shipped-surface audit is sufficient and treat the reshaped schemas, removed exports, and generated vintage metadata as the new supported contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The branch author assembled the stated shipped-surface audit and touched the central protocol-policy paths; a protocol owner should confirm the product decision.
